records.quote:
This vampire is born into certain aged families, and naught but
     death can destroy it. It is not conscious of its blood-madness,
     and acts only in a psychic state. The medium, also, is unaware
     of its terrible role
records.paraphrase: The text states this vampire is hereditary, only destroyed by death, and acts unconsciously, with both parties unaware of their roles.

records.quote:
Don't be a fool! You read that book! You know what relation you are to
me! I'd always hoped it was Cecilia, but now I know it's you.
records.paraphrase: Henry realizes his son is the 'medium' described in the book and demands to be tied down.

records.quote:
Arthur suddenly drew back at that odor--drew back with a gasp of awful
fear. For he recognized it--that stench, the heaviness of his blood, the
rawness of his tongue and gums.... Age-long it seemed, yet rising like a
spirit in his memory. All of these things he had known and felt before.
records.paraphrase: Arthur recognizes the physical symptoms that match the book's description of the medium's reactions.

records.quote:
Tie me to the bedposts, Arthur," came the command. "Tie both my hands
and both my feet.
records.paraphrase: Henry orders his son to bind him to the bed to prevent harm.

records.quote: Almost immediately he emptied both barrels of the shotgun into his head.
records.paraphrase: Arthur kills himself with a shotgun after discovering his father's death.

records.quote:
But in Heaven's name, Father, I've outgrown those things as I have
outgrown my clothes. I'm a man now; do you understand that? A man, with
a man's sense of logic.
records.paraphrase: Arthur contrasts his childhood superstitious fears with his adult rational, logical outlook.

records.quote:
As in the case of Autiel Duryea we observe that this specimen
     of _vrykolakas_ preys only upon the blood in its own family. It
     possesses none of the characteristics of the undead vampire,
     being usually a living male person of otherwise normal
     appearances, unsuspecting its inherent demonism.
records.paraphrase: A quasi-scholarly text describes a specific kind of vampire that only preys on its own family and appears as a normal living male unaware of his condition.

records.quote:
When these two outcasts are within a certain distance of each
     other, the coalescence of inherent demonism is completed, and
     the vampire is subject to its attacks, demanding blood for its
     sustenance.
records.paraphrase: The text describes proximity between the two family members completing the process and driving the vampire to seek blood.

records.quote:
I know, as any sane man would know, that you are neither a
vampire nor a murderer.
records.paraphrase: Arthur declares his father is neither a vampire nor a murderer.

records.quote:
The coroners who examined those tiny cadavers found them both dry of
all their blood, but could find no blood on the floor of the nursery nor
in the cradles.
records.paraphrase: Coroners' examination found the infant corpses drained of blood with none found spilled nearby.

records.quote:
But the death of Doctor Henry Duryea confronted the police with an
inexplicable mystery; for his trussed-up body, unscathed except for two
jagged holes over the jugular vein, _had been drained of all its blood_.
records.paraphrase: Henry Duryea is found dead, drained of blood despite being tied up, presenting an inexplicable death to police.

records.quote:
But this _vrykolakas_ cannot act according to its demoniacal
     possession unless it is in the presence of a second member of
     the same family, who acts as a medium between the man and its
     demon. This medium has none of the traits of the vampire, but
     it senses the being of this creature (when the metamorphosis is
     about to occur) by reason of intense pains in the head and
     throat.
records.paraphrase: The text explains the mechanism requiring a family 'medium' whose presence triggers the transformation and who senses it through head and throat pains.

records.quote:
That family rot is dispelled, Father. This is a civilized century.
Belief in vampirism is sheer lunacy. Wh-why, it's too absurd even to
think about!
records.paraphrase: Arthur insists that belief in vampirism is absurd in a modern civilized age.

records.quote:
All of France was doubtful, and even the savants who defended my name
at the trial found that they could not explain it nor disbelieve it. The
case was quieted by the Republic, for it might have shaken science to
its very foundation
records.paraphrase: Scholars at the trial could neither explain nor dismiss the deaths, and authorities suppressed the case for fear of undermining science.

records.quote:
His father had died during the night. He lay like a waxen figure tied to
his bed, his face done up in knots.
records.paraphrase: Arthur finds his father dead, still tied to the bed.

criteria.rationale: The story pseudo-scientifically frames hereditary vampirism as a heritable condition explained in quasi-scholarly terms, with references to shaking science 'to its very foundation.' However this is presented as demonic/supernatural (vrykolakas) rather than genuine speculative science, so materiality of an actual scientific representation is uncertain.
No engineered device, technique, or invention materially affects the setting or outcome. Ropes and a shotgun are ordinary tools, not inventions driving the plot in any technological sense.
The story is set in a contemporary 'civilized century' with historical references to ancestors, but there is no speculative future, remote past setting, or temporal displacement.

The tale develops systematic consequences from a stated premise (a hereditary vampire needing a family 'medium' whose proximity triggers metamorphosis), and the plot unfolds these rules to their fatal conclusion. Whether this counts as extrapolation from an identifiable scientific/social premise versus supernatural legend is uncertain.

Coroners and savants examine the bloodless corpses but explicitly cannot explain or test the phenomenon; no hypothesis-testing, measurement, or evidential revision materially drives understanding or action. The characters read a book rather than apply the scientific method.
There are no other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them; the demonic 'presence' is a supernatural/psychic conceit set entirely on Earth.

The deaths are personal tragedies—a father drained of blood and a son's suicide—confined to the last of a family line. Despite being fatal, they lack the large-scale (natural, technological, cosmic, biological, human-caused) disaster scope required; this is personal misfortune, not catastrophe.

candidates.description: A hereditary, quasi-scientific form of familial vampirism (vrykolakas) governing the Duryea bloodline: an unconscious 'vampire' member who preys only on his own kin, and who can act only in the proximity of a second family member acting as a 'medium.' The condition is transmitted by heredity, operates in a psychic/unconscious state, is signalled by shared physiological symptoms (head/throat pain, blood heaviness, decay odor), and is destroyed only by death.

novelty.rationale: The candidate posits a totalizing difference from the empirical norm: a specific, rule-bound species of familial vampirism (vrykolakas) that reorganizes the entire logic of the Duryea family and culminates in blood-drained corpses and an inexplicable death (sfev-930aa0d76d7d1358). It is not a mere gadget but a world-altering condition governing lineage across five centuries.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The text presents a systematic, immanent account with pseudo-biological rules: heredity, a required medium, proximity-triggered 'coalescence,' shared symptoms, and clinical framing (coroners, autopsy, savants who 'could not explain it nor disbelieve it'). This gestures toward an imaginary-science/quasi-naturalized explanation. However, the same quasi-scholarly source repeatedly invokes 'demonism,' 'demon,' and 'psychic state' as the operative mechanism (sfev-60faf5d4ff2f4b76, sfev-2bc6442e4ecdb85c), and characters frame it as a curse/legend. The account is therefore poised between a naturalized systematic logic and an explicitly supernatural/demonic one, so cognitive validation cannot be resolved as clearly present.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The candidate determines the entire narrative logic. The father's dread, the twenty-year separation, the binding to the bed, the son's recognition as the medium, the father's death drained of blood, and the son's suicide all follow directly from the rules of this familial vampirism. It is the overriding governing structure, not an incidental device.

estrangement.rationale: Reader-facing contrast is foregrounded through Arthur's repeated modern rationalist framing (civilized century, man's logic, vampirism as lunacy) set against the storyworld's confirmation of the condition via blood-drained bodies and the inexplicable trussed-up death. Storyworld consequences include the exsanguinated infants, the father's death, and the double catastrophe. Character reactions (Henry demanding to be tied, Arthur recognizing the symptoms) register the estrangement without requiring surprise.
